title: New Attachment Fitting Standard for the Trimmable Horizontal Stabiliser Front Spar on ZEPHYR-24 Aircraft
abstract: Forged attachment lug and a machined backing plate replace the built-up front spar attachment of the ZEPHYR-24 trimmable horizontal stabiliser, raising the fatigue margin at the load introduction into fuselage section 19.

sections.reason: Re-analysis of the ZEPHYR-24 tailplane load spectrum for the extended-range variants showed the front spar attachment reaching its reserve factor limit at 68000 flight cycles, short of the design service goal now claimed for the type. The built-up fitting concentrates the introduction load into a single shear plane and its inspection requires the aft fuselage to be opened, which operators only do at a heavy check. No in-service cracking has been reported; the change was launched from analysis and from operator pressure to extend the airframe life.
sections.description: The built-up front spar attachment is replaced by the forged lug CI558884-44 and the machined backing plate D5510122974242, bolted through the fitting D5510127798904 into the section 19 frame. The joint is shimmed with a liquid shim rather than laminated shims and the washers AES722822-2A are changed to a thicker corrosion-resistant item under the nut face. The new arrangement introduces the load through two shear planes and moves the critical location away from the fastener hole to the lug radius, which is accessible for eddy current inspection without stripping the aft cabin. Drawings D55101240925 issue D and D55101256601 issue F carry the fitting geometry and the shim procedure. Access is through zones 331, 341 and 193 with the tailplane supported on trestles.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 8.7 kg per aircraft, close to the aft limit of the loadable range, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of 0.11 per cent MAC that must be reflected in the weight and balance manual. No electrical load change. The fitting is not interchangeable with the previous standard because the bolt pattern and the shim scheme differ. The inspection threshold moves from 24000 to 40000 flight cycles and the aft cabin no longer has to be stripped for access. AMM and IPC content for ATA 55-10 required update, and the aft fuselage access task in ATA 53-31 was simplified.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z11770 in March 2024. A retrofit bulletin exists but embodiment is a heavy-check activity of about nine days with the tailplane supported, and take-up is expected to be limited to operators extending the airframe life.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft mass addition, CG shift 0.11 % MAC, weight and balance manual updated
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11770; the forged lug is a long-lead item and buffer stock was built before cut-in
